speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and when did the bleeding and pain start?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the location and character of the pain, and have you noticed any vaginal discharge or fluid leaking? Given your history of a prior cesarean section, is the pain specifically focused in the area of your old surgical scar?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text: The severe pain combined with vaginal bleeding and a prior C-section is concerning for a uterine rupture. Is the pain constant and localized directly over your old surgical scar, and have you noticed any fluid leaking from the vagina? REQUEST TEST: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring: Shows recurrent variable decelerations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recurrent variable decelerations combined with your severe pain and bleeding are highly concerning for uterine rupture or placental abruption. Is the pain currently constant and unrelenting, and have you felt any sudden loss of fetal movement? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound: Suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the ultrasound findings of uterine wall disruption and hemoperitoneum, this is a surgical emergency consistent with uterine rupture. DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture
